First and foremost, table two of the document records that target nine, 10, and 11 have no dedicated unit or staff resources. Chair, these are the sustainable use targets, wild species, agriculture, fisheries, forestry, and nature's contributions to people. They are the targets on which African livelihoods most directly depend. A structure that leaves them unstuffed is not aligned with the framework as a whole. We ask that this gap be closed in the 2027-2028 budget. Second, on core mandates require core funding. The access and benefit sharing unit carries goal C, target 13, the Nagoya Protocol, the clearinghouse, compliance and digital sequence information, and no additional post is identified. We ask that this be reassessed. The global coordination entity should likewise be supported through the core budget as an interim measure. Reliance on voluntary funding for permanent secretariat functions undermines institutional continuity and institutional memory. Core mandates cannot rest on voluntary contributions. We would like to speak on the issue of coherence, understanding that policy responsibility for digital sequence information remains in the Access and Benefit Sharing Unit, while support for multilateral mechanism and the Cali Fund sits in the Mainstreaming Economy and Finance Unit. Given their collective importance to Decision 16/2, we seek clarification on the rationale for this arrangement. how coherence will be maintained across two units and whether parties were consulted. Thank you, Madam Chair. Fiji delivers this statement on behalf of its 14 member states, Pacific small island developing states. Madam Chair, decision 16/28 adopted less than two years ago reaffirmed the importance of full and effective participation of at least two delegates from developing country parties, in particular the least in developed countries and small and developing states. For us, we ask this meeting's close attention on this item because it determines whether we are in this room for all others. The documents before us propose as the first listed option for every subsidiary body meeting of the next biennium funding one delegate. That is the second meeting of Article J, the 29th substar and the eighth SBI. For the 18th Conference of Parties, the first option is two, where three were funded for the 17th. Chair, the specific small island developing states cannot accept that. It reduces an important consideration that this conference has reaffirmed, and it puts us into an administrative option. We ask this meeting to select options that are equitable and that can, for the record of the decision, be consistent with paragraph 33 of decision 16/28. We understand the pressure as well, Madam Chair, particularly in terms of the replenishment of the voluntary trust fund. But we ask this meeting to look at what sits alongside that. At the end of last year, three general trust funds held a cumulative net asset surplus of $18.2 million over and above the working capital reserve and decision 16/28 has already established the precedent of a drawing on unspent balances from prior financial periods. A defined share of that surplus should be transferred to the participation fund. It is difficult to explain to our capitals why money that cannot be spent on the conventions work is being held while parties least able to attend are being told to send one person. There is also a venue arithmetic. The estimate for holding the AGM meeting in Montreal is $1.5 million against $0.4 million in Rome. The difference of $1.1 million is more than $977,405 in the same document estimates for funding one delegate from every eligible party at that meeting. We ask that venue selection be assessed expressly against the effective participation consistent with decision 16/25 and 16/27. Madam Chair, we also question the architecture being proposed. three stand-alone subsidiary body meetings in Montreal or Rome, in Nairobi and in Bangkok, and then the Conference of Parties. That is four separate long-haul journeys for Pacific delegates in two years, and for delegations that are only often able to send one person, justified in part by a short participation in funding. Back-to-back scheduling reduces journeys and decision 16/24 gives us agreed procedures for online and hybrid participation that would reduce them further. This document weighs the secretariat's workload carefully, it does not weigh ours. We have three further requests. One, that the allocation of participation funding be reported by least developed country and small island developing state status. Two, that the meeting be told how many SEEDS delegates were funded to attend it and how much budget for Arvan since reporting cut off of 31st May excludes both. And three, on the functional review which proposes 10 new posts of which one concerns conference savings. We encourage constructive discussions on budget scenario and we note that in passing 14 approved posts are currently vacant. Thank you Madam Chair.
